title: openai-bridge: stabilize streamed responses, pass seed hints, and enforce structured toolcall routing
author: Maya Singh
description:
Motivation: Customers using the OpenAI-compatible bridge reported intermittent stream truncation, mismatched tool/function call boundaries, and a missing surface for seed/determinism hints and URI-level metadata passthrough. This PR stabilizes the streamed Responses compatibility path, introduces a small 'seed_hint' passthrough that maps to our internal determinism toggle, and tightens the function-call routing to prevent partial-tool payloads from reaching backends.

Summary of changes (single-string): Implement streaming chunk integrity markers and a reassembly helper in pkg/openai_compat/stream_repair.go; add a lightweight 'SeedHint' HTTP header and map to request.determinism.seed_hint in api/handlers/responses_compat.go; validate and coalesce tool/function call events in the compatibility layer to ensure a complete call object before proxying; add unit and integration tests that simulate delayed/fragmented SSE chunks; add docs and an example client for the new header and stable reassembly behavior.

Why this shape: We intentionally keep the compatibility layer idempotent and low-latency: the stream repair is a minimal-state reassembler that only buffers chunks up to a short timeout (configurable) and emits sequence-checked frames to the internal runtime. The seed_hint header is advisory and does not override model-side randomness when a model enforces a different determinism policy; it maps to our determinism hints used by routing and cache keys. Tool/function calls are now validated against a JSON-schema in the bridge before being forwarded to ensure downstream consumers don't get half-formed objects.

Checklist:
- [x] streaming reassembly helper implemented
- [x] seed_hint header passthrough and internal mapping
- [x] toolcall coalescing+schema validation
- [x] unit tests for stream fragmentation and timeout behavior
- [x] integration tests with the runtime mock and example client
- [x] docs and example snippet added to docs/openai-compat.md

Commit summary:
- 0a1f2b3: pkg/openai_compat: add stream_repair with SeqID checks and CRC guard
- 1b2c3d4: api/handlers: read "SeedHint" header and attach to compatibility request context
- 2c3d4e5: compat: add toolcall coalescer + JSON schema enforcement
- 3d4e5f6: tests/integration: add fragmented SSE and toolcall assembly tests
- 4e5f6a7: docs: openai-compat.md examples and migration note

Files changed (high-level):
- pkg/openai_compat/stream_repair.go (new) -- reassembly and validation helper
- api/handlers/responses_compat.go -- header handling, schema validation, routing hints
- compat/schemas/toolcall.json (new) -- minimal schema used for bridge validation
- tests/unit/openai/stream_repair_test.go -- unit coverage for buffer timeouts and bad frames
- tests/integration/openai/compat_stream_fragmentation_test.go -- end-to-end simulated SSE fragmentation against runtime mock
- docs/openai-compat.md -- brief section on SeedHint, streaming guarantees, and example client
- examples/compatible-function-calls.md -- example client flow showing reassembly resilience
- go.mod/go.sum updates for added test deps

Illustrative snippet (kept small):
- stream_repair guarantees: each chunk must include a seq_id and either full_frame:true or continuation:true. The reassembler will merge continuations until full_frame:true is seen or timeout. Example pseudo: 
  {seq_id:123, continuation:true, payload:"..."}
  {seq_id:123, full_frame:true, payload:"..."} 

Review conversation (summary thread stitched into one continuous narrative):
- Ava Patel: "Great direction. Can we avoid a global buffer limit that could OOM with adversarial clients? Suggest per-seq window + soft-limit eviction."
- Maya Singh (author): "Agreed, implemented per-seq window + configurable maxBytesPerSeq (default 256KB) and eviction policy that emits an incompleteness marker downstream for observability."
- Liam Chen: "SeedHint semantics need to be explicit in docs. Will this change cache keys?"
- Maya Singh: "Docs updated. SeedHint is advisory only; we use it in deterministic routing decisions and as part of cache key derivation when present — noted in docs and tests. It will not force determinism for models that ignore it."
- Sofia Romero: "Tests look good; please add an integration test where the bridge receives interleaved toolcall chunks from two concurrent sessions."
- Maya Singh: "Added test (compat_stream_fragmentation_test.go) covering interleaved sequences and ensured per-session seq tagging prevents cross-session contamination."
- Ava Patel: "LGTM after CI green and a brief changelog blurb."

CI summary: Build: pass, Unit tests: pass, Integration tests: pass, Lint: pass. One flaky test (tests/integration/openai/old_stream_retry_test.go) was flaky and unrelated; team filed a follow-up ENG-1501. All relevant checks for this PR passed on the final run.

Compatibility notes and migration guidance:
- This is additive for users of the OpenAI-compatible Responses path. Clients that already stream will see stronger continuity guarantees; the bridge may emit an explicit "incomplete_frame" event for severely fragmented inputs (monitoring surfaced).
- New header: SeedHint: string. Example: SeedHint: "seed-20260301-42". This header will be preserved and surfaced in request metadata and used for cache keys when present. Do not assume it guarantees byte-for-byte determinism with third-party models.

Release notes (brief):
- Stabilize OpenAI responses streaming by adding chunk reassembly and sequence checks
- Add SeedHint header passthrough to support client-side determinism hints and better cache routing
- Enforce complete tool/function call objects in the compatibility bridge to prevent partial-tool deliveries

Follow-ups:
- ENG-1501: flakiness cleanup for unrelated old stream retry test
- ENG-1512: telemetry knobs for counts of repaired frames and dropped seqs

Merge: Squash and merge to main. Merged at 2026-03-01 by Maya Singh.

Notes: kept the bridge changes narrowly scoped to avoid touching the runtime Erlang-style router; this preserves our ability to roll back the compatibility layer independently if any customers see regressions.
